title: Activation & Scale Readiness Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a compact, ops-friendly checklist and KPI tracker for shipping a feature that must scale quickly on Redwood Inference (hosted + dedicated + private). It focuses on what product-ops and on-call squads must verify pre-traffic, during ramp, and in a surge/rollback scenario. Treat as living — update with postmortems and load test results.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to feature releases that will receive >1k requests/min in first 24h, or that change inference routing/model variants.
- Covers rollout phases: canary (0-1%), ramp (1-30%), scale (30-100%) + contingency.
- Assumes engineering has validated model bundle on target runtime (serving-runtime) and provided perf profile (p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory).

Primary success metrics (quick reference):
- Latency p95 (ms) by route: target <= 250ms hosted, <= 300ms dedicated under committed load.
- Token cost delta vs baseline: <= +12% (Optimize recommendations expected).
- Error rate (5xx + inference errors): <0.5% during ramp.
- Throughput (requests/min sustained): matches reserve capacity with <=10% throttling.
- Quality regression signal (eval prompt set): automated check passes with no >3% drop in task-specific metric.

Preflight checklist (owners in parens):
- Model & runtime: verified quantization/variant, KV cache behavior documented, expected memory footprints attached (Eng - Serving Runtime).
- Perf profile: dev + staging upper-bound p50/p95 for production-like seq lengths (Eng - Bench).
- Load tests: run 3 sustained load tests (canary, ramp, scale shapes) with synthetic traffic + recorded real requests where possible (SRE). Attach logs (links).
- Canary plan: exact user segments, % ramp schedule, abort criteria defined (ProdOps).
- Capacity reservation: Dedicated pools or burst plan confirmed, autoscale knobs set, pool warming run (Infra).
- Observability: dashboards for token-level cost, per-route latency, per-model SLOs, trace links, error-breakdown panels (Observability).
- Alerting & escalation: alert channels, runbook links, paging thresholds defined (SRE + Product-Ops).
- Security & privacy signoff: no new PII paths, KMS/HSM keys validated (Security).
- Rollback/feature-flag: immediate toggle path, canary-to-zero plan, and fallback model ready (Product + Eng).

Canary criteria (stop / abort if any met):
- Sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 10m;
- Error rate spike > 1% for 5m;
- Quality regression on eval set > 3 percentage points;
- Cost per 1k tokens rises > 20% above projected.
If any abort criterion hit: pause traffic, set feature-flag to previous variant, page on-call SRE and Eng lead, run triage checklist.

Traffic ramp plan (example timeline):
- T0 (canary start): 0.5% traffic for 30m. Verify traces, alerts quiet, KPIs green.
- T0+30m: if green, 2% for 60m. Run synthetic failure injection (latency + partial drop) in staging mirror to validate fallbacks.
- T0+90m: if green, 10% for 2h with capacity probe to Dedicated pools.
- T0+3h: if green, 30% for 4h, then 60% for 2h. Final to 100% after additional verification windows.
Adjust ramp cadence based on SLO breathing room and user-impact sensitivity.

Surge scenarios & contingency thresholds (examples):
- Sudden traffic 3x above forecast sustained >10m: trigger surge playbook — engage infra to scale pools, enable burst capacity, temporarily tighten batching to reduce latency.
- Model quality drift detected post-launch: revert to baseline model variant, start immediate evaluation batch on recent payloads, notify customer success for high-impact customers.
- Cost runaway (unexpected token costs): cap per-route token budget, enable caching of common prefixes, and pause low-priority routes.

Operational runbook snippets (for paging flows):
1) On-call receives "p95 latency > 500ms" alert: check per-route dashboard, confirm whether spike correlates with a specific model variant or region. If model-specific, switch routing to fallback variant and page Eng on-call.
2) On-call sees "error rate > 1%": capture recent traces link, sample payloads, check model health endpoint, and scale up serving replicas if 502/503 originate from saturation.
3) If rollout abort: set feature-flag, run post-abort data capture job (trace + sample requests), file triage ticket with severity and attach preflight artifacts.

KPI tracker (to fill during rollout):
- timestamp, traffic %, p50 latency ms, p95 latency ms, error rate %, token cost delta %, throughput r/min, eval quality delta %, notes (who signed off).
(Keep as a small sheet; product-ops will own daily snapshot during first 72h.)

Communications & stakeholder cadence:
- Pre-launch: 24h pre-brief to GTM, CS, Eng leads, SRE with runbook and contacts.
- During ramp: 15m syncs for first 2h, 30m thereafter until scale. Triage channel pinned in Slack + incident bridge ready.
- Post-72h: debrief doc, collect metrics, action items, and update playbook.

Post-launch validation and cleanup:
- Run the evaluation harness against production samples for 24h to surface subtle regressions.
- Reconcile estimated vs actual token spend and file cost variance ticket if >10%.
- Archive canary telemetry, attach to release artifact in GitHub, and update model version tags.

Open questions & follow-ups (notes to self):
- Add a short preset for private deployments where network cold-starts add ~200ms — adjust canary lengths accordingly.
- Need a standard synthetic-scan for prefix cache effectiveness that product-ops can run pre-launch.
- Bake in Optimize recommended quantization profile in the perf profile step to reduce token cost drift.

Appendix: useful links and quick refs:
- Perf profile template: CONFLUENCE:serving-runtime/perf-profile-template
- Canary automation playbook (scripts): GITHUB:repo/ops-automation/actions/canary.yaml
- Postmortem template: CONFLUENCE:incidents/postmortem-template

Owners and immediate contacts:
- Product Ops lead: Maya Chen (owner)
- Serving runtime: Ben Thompson (eng lead)
- SRE on-call rotation: see SRE rota (link in Confluence)
- Observability: Priya Nair

End of playbook. Update after each major release and after any incident to keep thresholds realistic and the checklist battle-tested.
